items.stem: A patient with a prepregnancy BMI in the normal range asks how much weight she should gain during a singleton pregnancy. Which range does the nurse cite from national guidance?
key: 25 to 35 pounds
items.rationale_correct: Normal-BMI patients are advised to gain about 25 to 35 pounds per the IOM 2009 guidance. Principle: individualize gestational weight-gain targets by prepregnancy BMI.

rationale_distractors.11 to 20 pounds: The range for patients with obesity.
rationale_distractors.40 to 50 pounds: Exceeds recommendations for a normal-BMI singleton pregnancy.
rationale_distractors.Weight gain should be avoided: Unsafe; appropriate gain supports fetal growth.

items.stem: Select all appropriate nutrition teaching points for a pregnant patient.
options: Take the recommended folic acid daily
Avoid unpasteurized dairy and deli meats unless heated
Consume raw or undercooked eggs for protein
key: Take the recommended folic acid daily
Avoid unpasteurized dairy and deli meats unless heated
Limit high-mercury fish
Include adequate iron-rich foods
items.rationale_correct: Prenatal nutrition emphasizes folate, listeria precautions, mercury limits, and iron. Principle: prenatal food safety is as important as adequate intake.

rationale_distractors.Consume raw or undercooked eggs for prot: Raises foodborne-illness risk and is not recommended.

items.stem: A patient asks whether a medication is safe in pregnancy and points to an old 'Category C' label. How should the nurse explain current drug labeling?
options: Letter categories are still the official FDA system
The FDA replaced letter categories with narrative Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling
Category C means the drug is completely safe
All Category C drugs are contraindicated
key: The FDA replaced letter categories with narrative Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling
items.rationale_correct: The PLLR replaced the A/B/C/D/X letters with narrative risk information; letters persist only in older references. Principle: interpret current labels as narrative risk summaries, not letters.

rationale_distractors.Letter categories are still the official: They were removed by the PLLR.
rationale_distractors.Category C means the drug is completely: The letters never meant simple safety.

items.stem: Which medication class should the nurse recognize as fetotoxic and generally contraindicated in pregnancy?
key: ACE inhibitors and ARBs
items.rationale_correct: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are fetotoxic, especially in later pregnancy, and are avoided. Principle: flag renally active antihypertensives as pregnancy-contraindicated.

rationale_distractors.Acetaminophen at recommended doses: Generally considered acceptable for pain or fever.
rationale_distractors.Iron supplements: Used to treat or prevent anemia.

items.stem: For each report, indicate whether it is a Normal discomfort of pregnancy or a Warning sign requiring prompt evaluation.

rows: Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day
Severe persistent headache with visual changes

items.rationale_correct: Severe headache with visual change, bleeding, and sudden facial/hand edema are warning signs; mild dependent swelling and heartburn are normal. Principle: severity, suddenness, and location separate danger from normal discomfort.

rationale_distractors.(any swap): Calling a warning sign 'normal' risks missing preeclampsia or hemorrhage; calling normal heartburn a warning sign causes needless alarm.

items.stem: Highlight the warning signs in this triage call note that require prompt evaluation. '28 weeks, reports mild nasal congestion, a severe headache that will not go away, blurred vision, mild ankle swelling, and sudden swelling of the face and hands.'
options: severe headache that will not go away
sudden swelling of the face and hands
key: severe headache that will not go away
blurred vision
sudden swelling of the face and hands
items.rationale_correct: Severe persistent headache, visual change, and sudden facial/hand edema suggest preeclampsia and need urgent evaluation. Principle: cluster these signs together — they point to one dangerous diagnosis.

rationale_distractors.mild nasal congestion: A common benign discomfort (rhinitis of pregnancy).
rationale_distractors.mild ankle swelling: Normal dependent edema, unlike sudden facial/hand swelling.

items.stem: A prenatal patient calls the triage line with several complaints. Rank these reports from highest to lowest priority for the nurse to address.
key: Vaginal bleeding with cramping
Severe headache with blurred vision
Mild constipation
Occasional round ligament twinge
items.rationale_correct: Bleeding and neurologic warning signs outrank benign discomforts; both danger signs are addressed before constipation or ligament pain. Principle: triage by threat to mother and fetus, not order of mention.

rationale_distractors.Mild constipation / round ligament twing: Both are normal discomforts, correctly ranked lowest, not urgent.

items.stem: During exercise, which symptom should the nurse teach a pregnant patient to stop and seek evaluation for?
key: Vaginal bleeding or fluid leakage
items.rationale_correct: Bleeding or fluid leakage during exercise is a stop-and-evaluate warning sign; mild heart-rate rise and perspiration are expected. Principle: teach the specific stop-exercise danger signs.

rationale_distractors.Feeling warm: Normal with activity; overheating specifically is the concern.

items.stem: A patient in the first trimester reports nausea. Which self-care measure should the nurse suggest first?
options: Eat small, frequent, bland meals and crackers before rising
Take an antiemetic before trying any dietary change
key: Eat small, frequent, bland meals and crackers before rising
items.rationale_correct: Small, frequent, bland meals and dry crackers before rising are first-line for mild nausea of pregnancy. Principle: start with dietary and behavioral measures before medication.

rationale_distractors.Skip breakfast entirely: An empty stomach often worsens nausea.
rationale_distractors.Take an antiemetic before trying any die: Medication follows non-pharmacologic measures for mild nausea.

items.stem: A patient planning to breastfeed asks about breast care in pregnancy. Which teaching is appropriate?
options: Vigorously scrub the nipples with soap to toughen them
Wear a supportive bra and avoid harsh soaps on the nipples
Apply alcohol to the nipples daily
key: Wear a supportive bra and avoid harsh soaps on the nipples
items.rationale_correct: Gentle breast care with a supportive bra and avoiding drying agents prepares for lactation. Principle: protect skin integrity rather than 'toughening' the nipples.

rationale_distractors.Express colostrum frequently before term: Not routinely advised and can stimulate contractions.

items.stem: Complete the counseling. A patient with a prepregnancy BMI in the obese range should be counseled to gain about [1] during a singleton pregnancy, and the nurse should [2].

2: individualize the plan and avoid dieting for weight loss
recommend fasting one day per week

key.2: individualize the plan and avoid dieting for weight loss

items.rationale_correct: Patients with obesity are advised to gain about 11 to 20 pounds, with an individualized plan and no intentional weight-loss dieting in pregnancy. Principle: adjust the target to BMI while still supporting fetal growth.

rationale_distractors.25 to 35 pounds / 40 to 50 pounds: Ranges for normal-BMI or excessive gain.

items.stem: Select all appropriate teaching points for common discomforts of pregnancy.
options: For heartburn, eat smaller meals and avoid lying down right after eating
For constipation, increase fiber and fluids and stay active
For back pain, use good body mechanics and supportive footwear
For leg cramps, point the toes downward and hold
For nausea, try small frequent bland meals
key: For heartburn, eat smaller meals and avoid lying down right after eating
For constipation, increase fiber and fluids and stay active
For back pain, use good body mechanics and supportive footwear
For nausea, try small frequent bland meals
items.rationale_correct: Evidence-based comfort teaching targets each discomfort; for leg cramps, dorsiflex (toes up), not point them down. Principle: match each discomfort to its specific relief measure.

rationale_distractors.For leg cramps, point the toes downward: Plantarflexion can worsen the cramp; dorsiflexion relieves it.

items.stem: What does the abbreviation PLLR stand for in current FDA medication labeling?
key: Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule
items.rationale_correct: PLLR is the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule, the narrative labeling that replaced the letter categories. Principle: know the current labeling system by name.

items.stem: A patient at 30 weeks calls reporting several symptoms. Which report should the nurse address as the highest priority?
options: Sudden gush of watery fluid from the vagina
Mild ankle swelling in the evening
key: Sudden gush of watery fluid from the vagina
items.rationale_correct: A sudden gush of fluid suggests preterm rupture of membranes and needs immediate evaluation. Principle: possible membrane rupture before term outranks benign discomforts.

rationale_distractors.Mild lower back ache: Common in pregnancy unless it becomes rhythmic pressure.

items.stem: A pregnant patient reports constipation. Which self-care measure should the nurse recommend first?
options: Increase dietary fiber, fluids, and activity
Begin a daily stimulant laxative indefinitely
key: Increase dietary fiber, fluids, and activity
items.rationale_correct: Fiber, fluids, and activity are first-line for constipation in pregnancy. Principle: use dietary and lifestyle measures before laxatives.

rationale_distractors.Begin a daily stimulant laxative indefin: Not first-line and not for indefinite use.

items.stem: A patient in an uncomplicated pregnancy asks about exercise. Which teaching is appropriate?
options: Most patients can do about 150 minutes of moderate activity weekly unless contraindicated
All exercise should stop during pregnancy
key: Most patients can do about 150 minutes of moderate activity weekly unless contraindicated
items.rationale_correct: Moderate activity (about 150 minutes weekly) is recommended in uncomplicated pregnancy. Principle: encourage safe activity while teaching the stop-exercise warning signs.

rationale_distractors.Only bed rest is safe: Bed rest is not routinely recommended.
rationale_distractors.High-risk contact sports are encouraged: Contact and fall-risk sports are discouraged.

items.stem: A patient reports following a strict vegan diet. Which nutrient deficiency should the nurse most specifically assess and counsel about in pregnancy?
key: Vitamin B12
items.rationale_correct: Vitamin B12 is found mainly in animal products, so a strict vegan diet risks deficiency that affects fetal neurologic development. Principle: match the deficiency risk to the dietary pattern.

rationale_distractors.Vitamin C: Abundant in plant foods, rarely deficient in vegans.
rationale_distractors.Sodium: Rarely deficient; excess is the more common concern.

items.stem: Which patient report during pregnancy should the nurse recognize as a warning sign of possible preeclampsia rather than a normal discomfort?
options: Mild swelling of the feet after standing
A severe, persistent headache with visual changes
key: A severe, persistent headache with visual changes
items.rationale_correct: A severe persistent headache with visual changes is a preeclampsia warning sign, unlike benign dependent swelling or heartburn. Principle: pair neurologic-visual symptoms with hypertensive disease.
